newsitem.title: HUNGARY: USAID helps Hungary to set up credit rating agency.
newsitem.headline: USAID helps Hungary to set up credit rating agency.

text.p: The Hungarian Bank Association (MBSZ) and USAID on Wednesday signed a cooperation agreement to help set up a Hungarian credit rating agency.

"This is an area where we think the United States of America has something to contribute," Thomas Cornell, representative of the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID), told the signing ceremony.
The agreement will make it possible to do research and train Hungarian specialists in the field of credit rating.
"The credit rating agency will help the Hungarian financial markets to receive independent assessment and analysis of risks, offering objective opinions...," the partners said in a statement.
Cornell told Reuters that USAID plans to spend $1 million to $1.3 million for the project which is supported by the Budapest Stock Exchange and by the MBSZ.

The assistance is part of the U.S government's efforts to help the democratic and economic transition of Hungary. Since the opening of its office in 1991 here USAID has provided over $210 million to Hungary, the statement said. @
The company is expected to operate as a shareholders' company with wide range of owners.
"Original ideas calls for...the widest possible circle of shareholders so that nobody should have a big stake, Miklos Pulay, General Secretary of MBSZ, said.
The new company may have up to 30 owners, including banks, brokerages, insurance companies, he said.
